hints.title: Zero In-Degree Necessity
hints.text: A node with no incoming edges cannot be reached from any other node. Therefore, every node with in-degree 0 must be included in the starting set.

hints.title: Sufficiency in DAG
hints.text: In a directed acyclic graph, every node can be reached by following paths backward to some node with in-degree 0.

hints.title: In-Degree Filter
hints.text: Collect all destination nodes in a set or boolean array. The answer is simply all nodes from 0 to n - 1 that never appear as destinations.

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating full reachability traversals from each node takes O(V * (V + E)).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking in-degrees in a boolean array takes O(V + E) time and O(V) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate proves that zero in-degree nodes are both necessary and sufficient in a DAG.
complexity.notes: Graph is guaranteed to be a DAG.
